suggested_visuals.section_heading: Does an Arcade Machine Actually Pay for Itself in a Bar?
suggested_visuals.purpose: Show the reader up front that a payback figure is the output of six named variables, not a fixed number
suggested_visuals.alt_text_proposal: Diagram showing six variables that determine arcade machine payback in a bar: foot traffic, venue type, revenue split, seasonality, maintenance, and electricity
suggested_visuals.production_note: Simple left-to-right flow diagram, six labelled inputs feeding one 'payback period' output box; neutral, non-salesy styling

suggested_visuals.section_heading: Comparing the Three Scenarios Side by Side
suggested_visuals.purpose: Let a skeptical operator see the payback spread between the three labelled scenarios at a glance
suggested_visuals.alt_text_proposal: Bar chart comparing illustrative arcade machine payback periods: 22 months pessimistic, 8 months neutral, 5 months optimistic
suggested_visuals.production_note: Three horizontal bars, months on the x-axis; include an on-chart note that all figures are illustrative planning assumptions

suggested_visuals.section_heading: Where a Machine Like the JVL Echo Fits Into the Math
suggested_visuals.purpose: Show the residential context clearly, so the home version is not visually confused with a commercial bar deployment
suggested_visuals.alt_text_proposal: Bartop arcade machine on a home bar counter in a warm basement lounge with two adults playing
suggested_visuals.production_note: Real photo of the ECHO Home unit in an adult residential space; warm evening lighting; no coin slot or bill acceptor visible in frame
